title.narrative: Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (UN Women Pilot)
Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (UN Women Pilot)

description.narrative: Impact: Furthest left behind women and girls in Palestine live a life free of violence. Outcome 1: Policy/decision makers' attitudes are more favorable towards the rights of furthest left behind groups of women and girls, survivors and victims of violence. Output 1.1: Knowledge and perception of policy/decision makers are enhanced and sensitized towards the rights of the furthest left behind groups of women and girls, victims and survivors of violence. Output 1.2: Women and human rights organizations are more capable to advocate for the rights of furthest left behind groups of women and girls, victims and survivors of violence. Outcome 2: Furthest left behind groups of women and girls access to quality and inclusive protection and reintegration services is enhanced. Output 2.1: Service providers develop and provide quality, accessible and more inclusive protection and reintegration services to the three identified groups of the furthest left behind groups of i) women and girls victims and survivors of violence (Girls in conflict with the law and victims and survivors of violence),ii) elderly women with disabilities, and iii) women and girls drug addicts. Output 2.2: Furthest left behind groups of women and girls (and their families) are more aware of their rights and the available services and how to use them. Output 2.3: Communities are supported to promote and uphold human rights of the furthest left behind groups of women and girls, survivors and victims of violence.

Det föreslagna projektet, Enhancing the Protection and Reintegration of Furthest Left Behind Groups of Women and Girls Victims and Survivors of Violence in Palestine (2020-2022) ska genomföras av UN Women i Palestina.
Programmet är väl i linje med stödområde 1 i den nya strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Palestina 2020-2024 "Mänskliga Rättigheter, demokrati, rättsstatens principer och jämställdhet", med huvudsyfte att åtgärda brister i policyer och tjänster för återintegrering och skydd. Det är ett pilotprojekt då det länkar samman tre områden inom samma stödområde: mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet och hälsa, vilket är ett relativt nytt sätt att arbeta inom ramen för strategin.

The proposed project, Enhancing the Protection and Reintegration of Furthest Left Behind Groups of Women and Girls Victims and Survivors of Violence in Palestine (2020-2022), is to be implemented by UN Women Palestine.
The project aligns with support area 1 of the new strategy for Sweden's international development cooperation with Palestine 2020-2024, 'Strengthened democracy, improved gender equality and greater respect for human rights', with the main objective of addressing the gaps in protection and reintegration policies and services. It is a pilot project in the sense that it interlinks the three areas under that support area: human rights, gender, and health, which is a relatively new approach within the strategy.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

title.narrative: Decision on contribution regarding "Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (Pilot Program with UN Women)"

description.narrative:
The overall goal of the programme was to enhance the protection and reintegration of the furthest left behind groups (FLBG) of women and girl victims and survivors of violence in Palestine, and the programme addressed the gaps in protection and services. There are many projects implemented in Palestine related to gender based violence, but the Shamlprogramme was unique since it focused on this specific group. The programme had a strategic approach working towards policy reforms by sensitizing policy and decision makers and establishing a better understanding of the needs of FLBGs. This was aimed at addressing legal and policies related to the target groups. UN Women has worked closely with the National Committee to Combat Violence against Women in Palestine (NCCVAW), the Ministry of Social Development, the Ministry of Womens Affairs and partners within the civil society. Civil society partners have been involved in advocating policy changes, as well as in service delivery and awareness raising.
At the policy level: The Shamlprogramme contributed to creating a more condusive environment for the inclusion of FLBG in protection schemes, both in relation to sheltering and to different key policies which have passed or is under revision. The decision by the former Minister of Social Development to revisit and amend the Cabinet's decision of 2011 was a breakthrough since FLGBs have been excluded from services. Other important changes have been the development of the new Violence Against Women Strategy (2023 2029) with focus on the right to protection for all groups of women the endorsement of the National Referral System of 2013 in line with the rights of women with disabilities the issuance of a Presidential decree amending the Penal Code No. 16 of 1960 and its amendments, which includes a definition of discrimination and criminalizing it the abolishing of Article 208 of the same law imposing a prison sentence on the perpetrators of torture crimes and those who order them or refrain from stopping them, and prohibiting torture on any basis. An endline survey concluded that 71 percent of policy and decisionmakers that was reached by the programme, are now willing to introduce policy reform that is inclusive to the rights of FLBG. Furthermore, a total of 772 (491 females 281 males) decision makers from different institutions and different capacities have increased their understanding and knowledge of the needs and rights of the FLBGs who are victims and survivors of violence. The decision makers participated and supported development and endorsement of other key policies and plans such as the development of National Strategy on persons with disabilities, the development of the new Strategy on Combating violence against women (2023 2029) with focus on the right to protection for all groups of women and the endorsement of the National Referral System of 2013 in line with the rights of women with disabilities amongst others.
At the service level: FLGBs affected by violence have not received relevant and adequate services. The programme has therefore addressed this in very concrete terms. With the help of the Shamlprogramme and support from decision makers and other institutions, seven service establishments have been adapted or established to meet the protection needs of these groups.These include: the establishment of a governmental shelter in Beitunia providing services to women sex workers and drug users the establishment of a new section for elderly women with disabilities inside the only governmental run elderly centre in Jericho the rehabilitation of the Girls Care Centre in Beit Jala the purchasing and operating of an elctronic system that serves cases of women users of drugs and women facing mental disorder in Gaza the creation of three safe spaces for women survivors of violence in three marginalized locations (refugee camps) in the West Bank Services have included psychosocial support, legal aid, medical services and dignity kits. Counselling sessions have covered topics related to FLGB's rights and available legal procedures. UN Women has reported a long list of women who have been reached by the programme, notably by the support through the civil society. For exampel a total of 9,047 women and girls of FLBGs accessed services during the programmes life cycle. A total of 518 service providers (461 females, 57 males) in the West Bank and Gaza have strengthened their knowledge and enhanced their skills in areas related to the management of cases of women of the FLBGs and the provision of gender responsive and inclusive services. For the work with elderly women with disabilities, UN Women has implemented direct support such as the refurbishment of the elderly centre in Jericho where a special section was prepared for elderly women with disabilities and a long term training was developed and delivered, targeting social workers, care givers and others. At another level, elderly women with disabilities received support through CSOs partners as they were targeted with awareness, psychosocial and legal aid services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
